paragraphs.text: A language with two thousand speakers, all of them over sixty, is in danger however many dictionaries exist. What matters is whether children hear it every day.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: One island tried nurseries where only the old language is spoken. Children learn it quickly, but they answer their parents in the national language unless the parents also use it at home.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Written material helps in a different way. Road signs and local news in the language tell speakers that it belongs in public life, not only at the kitchen table.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Success is slow to see. The island counts speakers every ten years, and the first rise came twenty years after the nurseries opened, when the first pupils had children of their own.
paragraphs.label: D
